opportunity: `kuna decompile-project` kept its own address-order schedule while `kuna decompile-all` decompiles callees first (option `protoorder`, on by default, #669). Both keep a `structsynth` ledger, and the ledger numbers a measured layout `struct_N` in the order the program is visited in, so the two surfaces put different records under the same name and nothing said so: on coreutils du -O2, 29 of the 30 synthesized names meant something else in the exported header than they did in `decompile-all --json`. The type campaign's own layout instrument reads types from one surface and layouts from the other, and that join is the whole of the round-C `structscore --layout` regression blamed on protoorder (results.md C.4).
status: Implemented. No new option: the behaviour is `protoorder`'s, and `--option protoorder off` gives `decompile-project` the old schedule exactly as it does `decompile-all`. `decompile-project --stream` (which writes each body as it finishes and cannot buffer a plan) and `decompile-graph` (one function per row) keep their schedules and still warn when the option is named.
refuted: results.md C.4's stated mechanism -- 'the callee's recovered pointer type wins the vote at the call site even where the caller measured the record itself'. With KUNA_SS_DEBUG instrumentation on `structsynth::accepts` and its install site, du -O2 installs 36 structures in each arm over the same bases; 32 of the 36 field lists are byte-identical and the other 4 differ only in a field's type spelling, never in an offset or a width. `hash_rehash`'s parameter measures {0,8,16,24,(32),40,48,56,64,72} in both arms. A caller's own layout already wins, because structsynth type-locks the parameter after the vote.
test_name: decompile_project_cli.rs (a_struct_name_means_the_same_record_in_the_export_and_in_decompile_all): every `struct struct_N { ... }` the export declares is the block `decompile-all --option structdefs on` prints for that name, in the default and the `protoorder off` arm. On protoorder_floatpointee_x86_64 three of five blocks disagreed before and none does after. tests/cli/sharded-project-export-keeps-serial-structs.json updated: the pool's replay line names `--jobs 1 --option protoorder off` and the parent prints the callee-first note.
